verses.text: “Then Heaven’s Kingdom will be like ten young women who took their lamps and went out to meet the groom.
Five were foolish; five were wise.
The foolish ones brought their lamps but didn’t bring extra oil.
The wise ones brought oil in jars along with their lamps.
The groom took a while, so all ten got sleepy and nodded off.
Around midnight, someone shouted, ‘Look! The groom’s coming! Come out and meet him!’ 🔔
All the young women woke up and got their lamps ready.
The foolish ones told the wise, ‘Share some oil with us; our lamps are going out.’
The wise replied, ‘There may not be enough for all of us. Go to the sellers and buy some for yourselves.’
While they were away buying oil, the groom arrived. Those who were ready went in with him to the wedding feast, and the door was shut.
Later the others came too, calling, ‘Sir, sir, open the door for us!’
But he answered, ‘I’m telling you the truth: I don’t know you.’
So stay alert, because you don’t know the day or hour the Son of Man is coming.
“It’s like a man going on a trip abroad. He called his servants and trusted them with his property.
He gave one five talents, another two, another one—each according to what they could handle. Then he left.
The servant with five talents got to work right away and earned five more.
The one with two did the same and earned two more.
But the servant with one went off, dug a hole, and hid his master’s money.
“After a long time, the master returned and settled accounts with them.
The servant who got five talents brought five more. ‘Master, you trusted me with five talents. Look, I’ve earned five more.’
“His master said, ‘Well done, good and faithful servant! You were trustworthy with a little; I’ll put you in charge of much more. Come share your master’s joy.’
“Then the servant who got two talents came. ‘Master, you trusted me with two talents. Look, I’ve earned two more.’
“His master said, ‘Well done, good and faithful servant! You were trustworthy with a little; I’ll put you in charge of much more. Come share your master’s joy.’
“Then the servant who got one talent came and said, ‘Master, I knew you’re a hard man: you harvest where you didn’t plant and gather where you didn’t scatter.
I was scared, so I went and hid your talent in the ground. Here, you can have back what’s yours.’
“His master answered, ‘You wicked, lazy servant! So you knew I harvest where I didn’t plant and gather where I didn’t scatter?
Then you should’ve put my money with the bankers. When I came back, I could’ve collected it with interest.
So take the talent from him and give it to the one who has ten.
Everyone who has will receive more and have plenty. But from the one who has nothing, even what he has will be taken away.
Throw that useless servant into the darkness outside, where people weep and grind their teeth.’
“When the Son of Man comes in His glory with all the holy angels, He’ll sit on His glorious throne.
Every nation will gather in front of Him, and He’ll separate people from one another, like a shepherd separates sheep from goats.
He’ll put the sheep on His right and the goats on His left.
Then the King will tell the people on His right, ‘Come, you who are blessed by My Father. Receive the Kingdom prepared for you since the world was founded.
I was hungry, and you gave Me food. I was thirsty, and you gave Me a drink. I was a stranger, and you welcomed Me.
I had no clothes, and you clothed Me. I was sick, and you cared for Me. I was in prison, and you came to visit Me.’
“Then the righteous will answer, ‘Lord, when did we see You hungry and feed You, or thirsty and give You a drink?
When did we see You as a stranger and welcome You, or without clothes and clothe You?
When did we see You sick or in prison and come visit You?’
“The King will answer, ‘I’m telling you the truth: whatever you did for one of the least important of these My brothers, you did for Me.’
“Then He’ll say to the people on His left, ‘Get away from Me, you cursed ones, into the eternal fire prepared for the devil and his angels.
I was hungry, and you gave Me no food. I was thirsty, and you gave Me nothing to drink.
I was a stranger, and you didn’t welcome Me. I had no clothes, and you didn’t clothe Me. I was sick and in prison, and you didn’t visit Me.’
“Then they’ll answer, ‘Lord, when did we see You hungry, thirsty, a stranger, without clothes, sick, or in prison and fail to help You?’
“He’ll answer, ‘I’m telling you the truth: whatever you failed to do for one of the least important of these, you failed to do for Me.’
They’ll go away to eternal punishment, but the righteous to eternal life.”
